description: Evidence classes for UniProt per-residue functional annotations. The classification is by ECO code, which is a structured field, so no human judgement enters gold. Codes outside this table make the build refuse to emit gold rather than silently fall through to a default class.
functional_feature_types_rationale: The residue-level functional vocabulary. Chain, Helix, Beta strand and Turn are also per-residue features but describe secondary structure rather than function, so they are counted separately and excluded from the functional census.

eco_class_notes.experimental: A published experiment on this protein. ECO:0000269 is the manual assertion from experiment code.
eco_class_notes.structural: ECO:0007744 is combinatorial evidence used by UniProt to cite a specific PDB entry; the cited entry id is in the evidence record and is what makes structure-confirmation computable.
eco_class_notes.inferred: Asserted by sequence similarity (ECO:0000250/0000255/0000256/0000259), from a publication's statement rather than its experiment (ECO:0000303), or by curator reasoning (ECO:0000305).
eco_class_notes.none: The feature carries an empty evidence list. Not a class of evidence but the absence of one; counted separately because it is the strongest audit signal.

counting_rules.record_identity: A feature record is identified by (type, start, end, ligand ChEBI id, alternative sequence). Two UniProt records sharing all five are one record. This rule matters: a binding site for two different ligands at one position is two records, and two mutagenesis substitutions at one position are two records, while a byte-identical repeat is one.
counting_rules.position_unit: A position is counted once per feature type however many records touch it.
counting_rules.evidence_citation_unit: An (record, ECO code, source id) triple. A record citing two PubMed ids under one code contributes two citations.
counting_rules.feature_class: A record's census class is the strongest class among its citations, ordered experimental > structural > inferred, or none when it has no citations. One class per record, so the per-type class counts sum to the record count.
counting_rules.ligand_identity: A ligand is identified by its ChEBI id, not its name.
counting_rules.policy_admission: A record is admitted under a policy when AT LEAST ONE of its citations falls in an accepted class. This is deliberately not the same test as the record_class census: the census reports the STRONGEST class a record carries, so a record citing both a published experiment and a structure counts once as experimental, while a policy that accepts structural evidence admits it. Reporting one and computing the other would make the two blocks silently inconsistent, so both rules are stated.
